scope: Every torsion-free coefficient group G, every finite m-by-n system with full rational row rank, all nonzero invariant factors; solution in a torsion-free overgroup embedding G.
support: The stipulated unrestricted coefficient embedding into U does not assert a torsion-free solution. Full TFS is exactly G intersect T_omega(U)=1, for the standard credited torsion-free radical.

Every root relation adjoined in radical removal has exponent vector in the original rational row span. Thus simply reapplying the full-row-rank theorem is unavailable; this is a method obstruction, not a counterexample.

Chiodo’s credited P=<x,y,z|x^2,y^3,xy=z^6> gives a nonsingular input G*P with first radical quotient G*C6 and second G. It shows neither universal torsion-freeness nor one-step removal holds, but the system has a trivial-variable solution in G.

The same presentation with z as coefficient has no coefficient-preserving torsion-free solution, but its three equations in two unknowns violate nonsingularity. Root adjunction repairs the specific nonsingular augmentation; this is not full TFS.

Rational abelianization and KMR residual torsion-free-solvable detection constrain the possible kernel. Smith normal form does not supply word-level layering; the planar source has coefficient-only boundary and balanced disk counts; power-series methods retain embedding assumptions.

Arbitrary coefficient cardinality reduces to finitely generated coefficient subgroups via torsion-free amalgamation, and rectangular systems reduce to square ones. Neither is a substantial standalone contribution.
